name: WiseLending empty-pool share inflation through a direct WBTC donation
summary: MainHelper._cleanUp, run through the syncPool modifier on every WiseLending entry point, compares IERC20.balanceOf(address(this)) against totalPool plus totalBareToken and credits any surplus to both totalPool and pseudoTotalPool without minting shares, so an unsolicited token transfer is booked as pool income for existing shareholders. MainHelper.calculateLendingShares additionally returns the raw amount when totalDepositShares is at most 1, so the first deposit into an empty pool mints one share per wei. Two one-wei WBTC depositExactAmount calls left the WBTC pool with two shares and a pseudoTotalPool of two, a direct transfer of 49.99999998 WBTC then made _cleanUp value each of those shares at about 25 WBTC, and the inflated collateral let borrowExactAmount take every other asset the protocol held before the flash loan was repaid out of a geometric sequence of WBTC withdrawals.
notes: WiseLending is a non-proxy contract that inherits MainHelper, WiseCore and WiseLowLevelHelper into one immutable runtime. That runtime has no address slot and no self-destruct or upgrade path, and it hashes to the same value at its creation block 17865066 and at the pre-exploit block 18342120.

Quantities are WiseLending's own ERC20 balance deltas between block 18342120 and block 18342121, so the aToken amounts already net out the interest that accrued inside the transaction. The 50 WBTC Balancer flash loan is attacker-supplied and is not loss; WiseLending in fact ended the transaction 0.01503674 WBTC richer than it started, and that surplus is not netted against the depletion. aEthWETH is valued at the ETH price because Aave v3 aTokens are redeemable one for one against their underlying and DefiLlama publishes no separate quote for aEthWETH. The executing searcher's own realised take was 169.402969354568854988 WETH, about 261805 USD at the same ETH price, which is the figure the seed row rounded to 260000; the 262280.51 USD recorded here is the larger victim-side depletion. Every component is valued from a DefiLlama historical query taken at the anchor timestamp 1697207963; the datapoints DefiLlama returned for that query carry their own stamps between 1697207997 and 1697208522, all within ten minutes of the anchor. Recoveries after the fact, if any, do not reduce gross depletion under the methodology.

The transaction was executed by the coffeebabe.eth searcher through a TyForTheMEV() entry point rather than by the original attacker, so it may have been a frontrun; that does not change which code executed, the depletion measured, or the anchor, which is the earliest successful defect-executing transaction either way.
